goal: The vacation accessibility filter must return catalog places that carry the verified accessibility attribute.

intent_model.literal_request: Correct the accessibility feature association because the filter shows no results even though the attribute exists.
intent_model.implied_outcome: One canonical accessibility truth must flow from the supplier API through the compact catalog and every vacation search state.
likely_rejections: Only the reported desktop state is repaired
The filter relies on truncated card copy instead of the source attribute
The public site is claimed fixed without publication authorization or live evidence

interpretation_rules.operational_meaning: Treat the correction as a shared-contract regression and lock the causal boundary with tests.
interpretation_rules.acceptance_impact: Applied, draft, compact payload and reload states are all required.

cognitive_flow.current_layer: The person selects accessibility and sees actual matching places.
cognitive_flow.current_decision: Accessibility is either verified in the catalog or it is not; shortened card copy cannot override it.
cognitive_flow.next_action: Apply the filter and compare matching places.
deferred_complexity: Detailed accessibility arrangements remain on the place page when supplied.

natural_destination: Desktop and mobile vacation search with the accessibility filter applied.

facts.claim: The compact catalog contains 4 vacation places with searchFilterIds including accessible.
facts.evidence: Node diagnostic against app/data/sergey-public-catalog.json and publicVacationSearchProperties on 2026-11-03.

facts.claim: The current UI predicate finds 0 because compact card features contain only the first 3 display labels.
facts.evidence: The same diagnostic returned projectedVisibleExact=0 while projectedAccessibleIds=4.

assumptions.claim: The current bundled catalog represents the intended local release candidate data.
assumptions.validation: Verify the filter identity through the same public-catalog projection used by the app and inspect the local route.

in_scope: Canonical accessibility matching in applied vacation results
Canonical accessibility matching in draft filter preview
Regression tests for compacted feature data
invariants: Only supplier-derived verified accessibility attributes qualify
Other vacation filters keep their current behavior
No catalog, database or supplier mutation

requirements.statement: A verified accessible catalog property must remain filterable after compact projection.
Applied and draft filter states must use the same canonical accessibility predicate.
Unverified properties must not be included only because of unrelated display text.

acceptance_checks.observable_result: All properties carrying the accessible ID match even when their three display features omit accessibility.

acceptance_checks.setup: Open applied results and the draft filter drawer
acceptance_checks.observable_result: Both paths call the same canonical matcher and produce the same eligible set.

acceptance_checks.setup: Use a property without the accessible ID or a verified source label

acceptance_checks.observable_result: The filter stays selected and the verified result set remains nonzero.

acceptance_checks.setup: The repair causes an affected-family regression
acceptance_checks.observable_result: No supplier or catalog data rollback is required.

authorization_boundary: Local repair, verification and commit only. Publishing remains a separate explicit action.
